name: @hermitsh/shrimp-mcp

tools.name: shrimp_pair
tools.description:
Connect this agent to a SHrimp account using a 6-digit pairing code.

The user must open the SHrimp app on their phone → Settings → Agents → Pair New Agent to generate a code. The code expires after 5 minutes.

After pairing, this agent can read and write the user's task tree. The token is saved locally so you stay connected across sessions.

Args:
  - code (string): The 6-digit numeric code from the SHrimp app.
  - agentName (string): Display name for this agent in the app (default: "Claude").

Returns on success:
  { paired: true, email: string, agentName: string, scopes: string[], configPath: string }

Returns on failure:
  { paired: false, error: string }

Common errors:
  - "Invalid code" → code is not exactly 6 digits
  - "Pairing failed" → code expired or wrong. User must generate a new one.

code.description: The 6-digit pairing code from the SHrimp app

agentName.description: Display name for this agent connection (shown in the SHrimp app)

tools.name: shrimp_status
tools.description:
Check whether this agent is paired with a SHrimp account.

Takes no arguments.

Returns:
  { paired: true, email: string, agentName: string, scopes: string[] }
  or
  { paired: false }

If not paired, call shrimp_pair with a 6-digit code from the user's SHrimp app.

tools.name: shrimp_get_tasks
tools.description:
Read the user's task tree from SHrimp.

Returns all tasks as a nested hierarchy. Each task has: id, title, notes, dueDate, category, isCompleted, isArchived, and children[].

Filters (all optional):
  - category: one of home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects
  - completed: "true" or "false" — filter by completion status
  - archived: "true" or "false" — default is active only (false)
  - subtree: a task ID — returns only that task and its descendants
  - flat: "true" — returns a flat array with parentID instead of nesting

The response includes a version number. Cache this to detect changes efficiently.

Returns:
  { version: number, updatedAt: string, tasks: TaskItem[] }

TaskItem shape:
  { id: string, title: string, notes?: string, dueDate?: string, category?: string, isCompleted: boolean, isArchived: boolean, children: TaskItem[] }

category.description: Filter by category: home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects

archived.description: Filter by archive status (default: active only)

subtree.description: Task ID — return only this task and its descendants

flat.description: Return flat list with parentID instead of nested tree

tools.name: shrimp_search
tools.description:
Search tasks by keyword. Matches against titles and notes (case-insensitive substring match).

Returns matching tasks with their full breadcrumb path so you know where they sit in the tree.

Args:
  - q (string): Search query.
  - limit (number): Max results, 1–50 (default: 20).

Returns:
  { results: SearchResult[], total: number }

SearchResult shape:
  { id: string, title: string, notes?: string, isCompleted: boolean, path: string[], matchField: "title" | "notes" }

tools.name: shrimp_add_task
tools.description:
Create a new task in SHrimp. The task appears on the user's phone within seconds.

You can nest tasks at any depth by specifying a parentID. Use insertBefore to control ordering among siblings.

Args:
  - title (string, required): Task title.
  - notes (string, optional): Additional notes or details.
  - parentID (string, optional): UUID of parent task. Omit for a root-level task.
  - dueDate (string, optional): ISO 8601 date (e.g. "2026-04-15").
  - category (string, optional): One of home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects.
  - insertBefore (string, optional): UUID of sibling task to insert before.

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

Tips:
  - Use shrimp_batch for creating multiple tasks at once (up to 50 ops).
  - UUIDs must be hex-only (0-9, a-f). Non-hex characters will be rejected.

parentID.description: UUID of parent task (omit for root-level task)

category.description: Category: home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects

insertBefore.description: UUID of sibling task to insert before

tools.name: shrimp_update_task
tools.description:
Update an existing task's properties. Only include the fields you want to change — omitted fields are left unchanged.

Args:
  - taskID (string, required): UUID of the task to update.
  - title (string, optional): New title.
  - notes (string, optional): New notes (replaces existing notes entirely).
  - dueDate (string, optional): New due date (ISO 8601).
  - category (string, optional): New category (home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects).

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

taskID.description: UUID of the task to update

category.description: New category: home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects

tools.name: shrimp_complete_task
tools.description:
Toggle a task's completion status. If incomplete, marks it done. If already done, marks it incomplete.

Args:
  - taskID (string, required): UUID of the task.

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

taskID.description: UUID of the task to complete/uncomplete

tools.name: shrimp_archive_task
tools.description:
Archive a task and all its children. Archived tasks are hidden from the main view but not deleted. Use shrimp_restore_task to bring them back.

Args:
  - taskID (string, required): UUID of the task to archive.

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

taskID.description: UUID of the task to archive

tools.name: shrimp_restore_task
tools.description:
Restore an archived task back to the active list.

Args:
  - taskID (string, required): UUID of the task to restore.

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

taskID.description: UUID of the task to restore

tools.name: shrimp_move_task
tools.description:
Move a task to a different position in the tree. Can reparent under a new task or reorder among siblings.

Args:
  - taskID (string, required): UUID of the task to move.
  - parentID (string, optional): UUID of new parent. Omit or null to move to root level.
  - insertBefore (string, optional): UUID of sibling to insert before. Omit to append at end.

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

Tips:
  - Moving a task also moves all its children.
  - You cannot move a task under itself (circular reference).

taskID.description: UUID of the task to move

parentID.description: UUID of new parent (omit to move to root)

insertBefore.description: UUID of sibling to insert before

tools.name: shrimp_delete_task
tools.description:
Permanently delete a task and all its children. This cannot be undone by the agent (the user can undo on their phone within a short window).

Prefer shrimp_archive_task if you're unsure — archived tasks can always be restored.

Args:
  - taskID (string, required): UUID of the task to delete.

Returns:
  { ok: true, opID: string, version: number }

taskID.description: UUID of the task to delete

tools.name: shrimp_batch
tools.description:
Execute multiple task operations in a single request. Much more efficient than individual calls when making several changes at once.

Max 50 ops per batch. All ops are validated upfront before any are applied — if one has an invalid UUID, the entire batch is rejected.

Each op must have a "type" field. Required fields depend on the type:
  - create: title (required), notes, parentID, dueDate, category, insertBefore
  - update: taskID (required), title, notes, dueDate, category
  - complete: taskID (required)
  - archive: taskID (required)
  - restore: taskID (required)
  - move: taskID (required), parentID, insertBefore
  - delete: taskID (required)

Args:
  - ops (array): Array of operation objects (max 50).

Returns:
  { ok: true, opIDs: string[], version: number }

Tips:
  - Use this to build entire project plans in one call.
  - Create ops are processed in order, so you can create a parent then nest children under it in the same batch.
  - All UUIDs must be hex-only (0-9, a-f).

category.description: One of: home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects

tools.name: shrimp_get_prompt
tools.description:
Read the current prompt sections that control the in-app AI behavior. SHrimp's AI system prompt is modular — split into 6 editable sections that shape how the AI processes user requests.

Sections:
  - intro: Identity and role definition
  - rules: Behavioral rules and constraints
  - thoroughness: How thorough/detailed the AI should be
  - categories: Life categories for task organization (home, work, errands, health, people, money, travel, projects)
  - schema: The JSON response schema the AI must follow
  - terminal: Additional instructions for the terminal/chat interface

Returns all sections with their current content. Empty strings indicate the section uses the built-in default.

Use this to understand the current AI behavior before making changes.

tools.name: shrimp_update_prompt
tools.description:
Update one or more prompt sections that control the in-app AI behavior. Partial updates are supported — only include the sections you want to change.

Sections: intro, rules, thoroughness, categories, schema, terminal

This immediately pushes the changes to the user's phone. The next AI request will use the updated prompt.

Rate limit: 20 settings changes per hour.

Example: To make the AI more concise, update the "thoroughness" section.
Example: To add a new category, update the "categories" section.
Example: To change how the AI introduces itself, update the "intro" section.

IMPORTANT: Read the current sections first (shrimp_get_prompt) before making changes, so you understand what you're modifying.

thoroughness.description: How thorough/detailed the AI should be

schema.description: JSON response schema the AI must follow

tools.name: shrimp_get_provider
tools.description:
Read the current AI provider and model configuration. This controls which AI processes requests in the SHrimp app.

Returns:
  - type: The provider (anthropic, openai, google, xai)
  - modelID: The specific model ID (e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "gpt-4o")
  - useOpenAIOAuth: Whether OpenAI uses ChatGPT OAuth (true) or API key (false)

tools.name: shrimp_update_provider
tools.description:
Change the AI provider and/or model used by SHrimp. This immediately pushes the change to the phone.

Valid providers: anthropic, openai, google, xai

You can update just the provider, just the model, or both. The user must have an API key configured for the selected provider (this tool cannot set API keys).

Rate limit: 20 settings changes per hour.

Example: Switch to Anthropic's Claude → type: "anthropic", modelID: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
Example: Switch to OpenAI → type: "openai", modelID: "gpt-4o"

useOpenAIOAuth.description: Use ChatGPT OAuth instead of API key (OpenAI only)

tools.name: shrimp_pipeline
tools.description:
Read the processing pipeline log from the user's phone. This shows what the in-app AI has been doing — push notifications received, emails fetched, AI requests sent, inbox status transitions, etc.

The pipeline is a ring buffer of up to 200 entries, synced to the server when the app launches and periodically during use. Entries are chronological (oldest first).

Pipeline stages:
  - push: Push notification received
  - fetch: Full email body fetch
  - attach: Attachment fetch/cache
  - batch: Inbox batch processing
  - ai: AI request/response/error
  - inbox: Inbox status transitions
  - share: Share extension receive
  - file: Disk read/write operations
  - retry: Crash recovery re-queues

Use this to understand what's happening on the phone, debug issues, or monitor AI activity.

The pipeline naturally reflects changes made by outside agents — when you modify tasks, the phone processes those changes and logs them here.

tools.name: shrimp_inbox
tools.description:
Read the SHrimp terminal inbox. The inbox receives items from multiple sources — emails, share extension, Siri, GitHub webhooks, and the in-app composer. Each item is processed by the phone's AI to create/update tasks.

Item sources: email, shareExtension, siri, github, clipboard, composer

Item statuses:
  - pending: Saved but not yet sent to AI
  - processing: Currently being processed by AI
  - processed: AI successfully handled it
  - failed: AI call failed (check failureReason)

Attachment metadata is included (filename, type, size) but not binary data.

Items are returned newest first. Use filters to narrow results.

tools.name: shrimp_feedback
tools.description:
Send feedback to the SHrimp developer on behalf of the user. This works like the feedback button in the app's settings — your message is stored and forwarded to the support team.

Use this when:
  - The user asks you to report a bug or issue with SHrimp.
  - The user wants to suggest a feature or improvement.
  - You notice something that seems like a bug while interacting with SHrimp.

Rate limit: 5 feedback messages per hour.
